title: Quantitative validator coverage matrix for misconfiguration classes across vendors (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Which classes of injected misconfiguration in LLM-generated network artifacts are detected by a baseline validator suite (validator-only) versus a guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation), and what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) aggregated across vendors and topology templates?
confirmatory_hypotheses: Primary (confirmatory): The guarded pipeline (validator + automated sandboxed emulation) will detect a higher proportion of injected misconfigurations than the baseline validator-only pipeline. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across all injected samples; preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 (20 percentage points).

Secondary (exploratory): Detection gaps will be nonuniform across misconfiguration classes (syntax, ACL semantics, routing loop/break, VRF/tenant isolation violations, control-plane inconsistencies, vendor-CLI misuse) and vendor-CLI families.
exploratory_questions: Which specific validator rule IDs or emulation observation types account for most additional detections by the guarded pipeline?
Are there classes or vendors where the guarded pipeline provides negligible benefit (paired difference ≈ 0)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic LLM-generated network configuration artifacts (intent→config) produced via hosted LLM API(s) permitted by the capability manifest
Three vendor-CLI families (vendor A, vendor B, vendor C; vendor labels used abstractly to preserve reproducibility of CLI families rather than proprietary names)
A small set of topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, simple triangle) represented as input topology manifests used for generation and emulation
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across all injected samples (guarded minus baseline detection proportion)
secondary_estimands: Counts of emulation-confirmed false negatives for the baseline validator (per class/vendor)
sampling_plan: Paired design. For each task (N=720 confirmatory tasks) a single shared initial model generation is produced (per registered adapter contract: one initial generation per task, shared across the two paired conditions). For each generated config sample that passes vendor-specific parser checks (inclusion), run (1) baseline validator-only pipeline and (2) guarded pipeline (baseline validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation). Outcome per sample is binary: detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1} and detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}. Parser failures trigger the deterministic missingness handling policy (automatic reseed up to two times; irrecoverable failures replaced per missingness_plan). Runtime model sampling parameters (provider-returned sampling metadata) will be recorded in the execution manifest for every generation; no claim of deterministic model sampling is made.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: 0.20 absolute increase. Recommended scenario: 3 vendors × 6 classes × 40 per-cell = 720 confirmatory samples (task_count=720) plus discovery pilot (80 items) for taxonomy and mapping validation. Power calculation used an approximate paired-binary formula (McNemar-type / paired-proportion approximation) to target ≈80% power under baseline aggregated detection rate assumptions 40%–60% and conservative intracluster correlation ≤0.05. Alpha = 0.05 (two-sided) for the primary aggregated estimand. Sensitivity analyses: (a) treat irrecoverable technical failures as nondetections (conservative), (b) stratified paired estimates by class and vendor (exploratory), (c) bootstrap cluster-robust CIs by topology template. Calculation details and assumptions will be saved in the execution manifest.
exclusion_rules: Exclusion: generated artifacts that fail vendor-specific parser checks after allowed automatic reseeds (parser failures → deterministic reseed up to two times; irrecoverable parser failures are treated as technical exclusions and replaced deterministically prior to analysis).
Duplicate artifact hash collisions detected by provenance hashing → automatic exclusion and deterministic reseed per contamination_plan.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (parser failures, emulation harness crashes, provider timeouts) are handled deterministically: up to two automatic re-executions per sample; if still failing, the sample is replaced by deterministic reseed using stored PRNG seed and recorded as a technical exclusion. Primary analysis excludes irrecoverable technical pairs per the paired_binary_analysis_v1 contract's default (complete_pair_primary). A pre-registered sensitivity analysis will treat irrecoverable failures as nondetections in the guarded pipeline (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity). All failures, reseeds, and replacements are logged in the execution manifest.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis will be executed via the registered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 (primary_estimand_id = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Compute the aggregate paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) across all confirmatory samples with 95% confidence intervals using the executor's default paired-binary procedures (McNemar-style / paired logistic with cluster-robust SE for topology clusters). Primary-call failure treatment: use paired_binary_analysis_v1 allowed options; primary plan uses complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs) and a pre-registered sensitivity analysis using complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity. Secondary analyses: per-class and per-vendor paired analyses (exploratory) with Bonferroni-adjusted CIs as per multiplicity_plan. All analysis code, execution manifest, and seeds will be recorded and published.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is the aggregated paired detection-rate difference across all confirmatory samples. Secondary per-class and per-vendor comparisons are exploratory and will be reported with Bonferroni-adjusted confidence intervals (family-wise alpha corrected for number_of_classes × number_of_vendors = 6 × 3 = 18 tests) and explicitly flagged as exploratory. No hierarchical gate-rejection is required for the primary aggregated estimand.
contamination_plan: {"benchmark_names": ["LLM-generated synthetic NetOps misconfig coverage"], "risk_factors": ["Duplicate seeds or accidental reuse of generated artifacts across discovery and confirmatory sets", "Leakage of prompt templates or injected fault templates into model prompt history (if hosted API had caching)", "Validator rule-set updates between discovery and confirmatory runs"], "detection_procedures": ["Deterministic artifact hashing (SHA-256) for every generated sample and input seed fingerprinting; any hash collision auto-flagged", "Prompt and artifact provenance logging with immutable timestamps; automated diff-based detection of template reuse", "Automated validation that validator binary/config version hashes match preregistered values before confirmatory execution"], "item_flagging_rules": ["Duplicate artifact hash → automatic exclusion and deterministic reseed", "Any validator or emulator binary/config checksum mismatch → automatic halt to confirmatory execution until corrected; mismatched run flagged as invalid", "Prompt-template divergence from preregistered templates beyond exact-token tolerance → automatic exclusion"], "analysis_treatment": "Flagged contaminated items are excluded and replaced deterministically prior to analysis. All contamination flags and replacements are recorded in the execution manifest. Sensitivity analysis will report results including and excluding replaced items.", "residual_uncertainty": ["Potential hidden caching or provider-side non-determinism in hosted LLM API not detectable by client-side checks", "Unobserved differences between emulation runs and some vendor production behaviors"]}
stopping_rule: No interim analyses or early stopping for efficacy. Execution stops when all preregistered confirmatory tasks (task_count=720) have produced valid paired outcomes or when a critical contamination/validator-version mismatch is detected (in which case confirmatory execution halts until the mismatch is resolved per contamination_plan). Technical retries per sample are limited to the missingness_plan.
planned_outputs: IEEE-format short paper (≤5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement
Execution manifest (hashes, seeds, runtime sampling metadata, model identifiers, binary checksums)
Raw generated artifacts, emulation traces, validator outputs, and mapping tables (public dataset release subject to provider TOS)
Analysis code and final results (point estimates, 95% CIs, sensitivity analyses)
Evidence-to-claim table and autonomous revision log
